project.objective: Did Friedrich Carl Weber and his wife Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau have a daughter named Anna Maria Eva, born 1870?

questions.question: Did Friedrich Carl Weber and his wife Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau have a daughter named Anna Maria Eva, born approximately 1870?
questions.rationale: This is the project's central question — a parentage and birth relationship question for a specific child in a German Lutheran community in Sindlingen (near Frankfurt), Hesse-Nassau. Civil registration (Standesamtsbücher) began in Hesse-Nassau in 1876; church registers (Lutheran Kirchenbücher) for Sindlingen predate that and survive for the 1870 period, making this testable. FamilySearch holds digitized German church and civil records for this region. The question is framed at the objective's own scope: was Anna Maria Eva, born ~1870, a daughter of this specific couple?

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three Catholic church records from FamilySearch collection 3479701 (Germany, Hesse-Nassau, Diocese of Limburg, Catholic Church Records, 1601-1919) provide two independent evidence units that directly answer the parentage question. The first unit — records D43H-7DN2 and D43D-J2MM, two indexing passes of the same baptism register entry — records Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 Feb 1870, baptized 13 Mar 1870 at Höchst, daughter of Karl Weber (Friedrich Carl Weber's working name) and Katharina Karell (= Catharina Carell). The second unit — record D4WC-V9PZ, the baptism of sibling Rosina Weber, 3 May 1869 at Nied/Höchst — independently names the father as 'Carl Friedrich Weber' (both given names, reversed order) and mother 'Catharina Karel.' The distinctive surname Carell/Karell/Karel is consistent across all three separate register entries. The family is demonstrably Catholic (all baptisms in Catholic parishes), making the Sindlingen Lutheran register irrelevant to this family. Civil registration did not begin in Hesse-Nassau until October 1874, so no civil birth certificate exists for the 1870 birth. FamilySearch indexed collections 1768560, 3015626, and 1473000 were searched and confirmed to lack Sindlingen-specific indexed entries. Browse-only volumes (pli_009, pli_010, pli_011) were skipped due to a missing OpenRouter API key — a tool-environment limit, not source destruction or a privacy seal — but the images remain accessible interactively. The accessible indexed evidence supports a defensible conclusion; original image examination and the marriage register (pli_010) would advance tier but are not required to sustain the parentage finding. No conflict is registered. Overturn risk is low: no unsearched source is likely to name a different father given the distinctive surname correspondence and independent sibling corroboration.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. Record D43H-7DN2/D43D-J2MM (one evidence unit) records the baptism of Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 Feb 1870, daughter of Karl Weber and Katharina Karell, at Höchst — directly answering the parentage question. Record D4WC-V9PZ independently names the father as 'Carl Friedrich Weber' and mother 'Catharina Karel,' providing a second, corroborating evidence unit. The question is answered affirmatively.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Substantially met. Four FamilySearch indexed collections were searched (1768560, 3015626, 1473000, 3479701). The decisive collection 3479701 yielded Anna Maria Eva's baptism record and a sibling record. The Sindlingen Lutheran browse-only register (pli_009) was not read due to a missing OpenRouter API key, but the family demonstrably baptized at Catholic parishes (Höchst and Nied/Höchst), making that Lutheran volume inapplicable to this family. The marriage register (pli_010) and confirmation register (pli_011) were similarly blocked. OFB and Ancestry searches were deferred. The critical record type — Catholic baptism register for the Höchst/Limburg diocese — was searched and returned positive results. Note: interactive examination of the original images and the marriage register would strengthen the conclusion further.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Partially met. The assertions derive from FamilySearch indexed entries (derivative of the original parish register), not from direct image examination of the underlying register pages. The original images are accessible at FamilySearch but could not be transcribed in the current tool environment (missing OpenRouter API key). Two independent indexing passes (D43H-7DN2 and D43D-J2MM) cross-check consistently, reducing the risk of transcription error. The marriage register image (pli_010) also was not examined. Original image review remains the outstanding step for full GPS tier compliance; the declaration proceeds on the accessible indexed evidence, which consistently and independently supports the parentage conclusion.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Records D43H-7DN2 and D43D-J2MM are two indexing passes of the same underlying register entry and constitute one evidence unit. Record D4WC-V9PZ is an entirely separate baptism register entry (sibling Rosina, born 3 May 1869, baptized at Nied/Höchst — a different date, different child, different baptism location, different presenting parents). These two evidence units are genuinely independent: different register entries, different informants, different occasions. Both name the same parents with consistent surname spelling.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Substantially met. Records D43H-7DN2 and D43D-J2MM are indexed derivatives of original Catholic parish registers — the christening assertions (a_004, a_015) carry information_quality 'primary' for the officiant-recorded baptism place and date. The parentage assertions carry information_quality 'indeterminate' (correctly classified: the presenting parent's identity of themselves is primary, but the informant's precise categorization is uncertain without the original image). Record D4WC-V9PZ provides a second original parish record with primary information from the officiant. The source base is original Catholic church records; the index-vs.-original gap (noted under original_substitution) is the limiting factor.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered. The name variants across records (Karl / Carl Friedrich / Friedrich Carl for the father; Katharina Karell / Catharina Karel / Catharina Carell for the mother) are consistent orthographic and given-name-order variants, explained by standard 19th-century German Catholic recording practice. The parish officiant's recording of given names in varying order is documented in the informant_bias_notes on the relevant assertions. No discrepancy remains unresolved.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Two independent evidence units from two separate Catholic register entries consistently name Anna Maria Eva Weber as the daughter of this specific couple. The distinctive and unusual surname Carell/Karell/Karel appears identically across all three records, making misidentification unlikely. The Sindlingen Lutheran register is inapplicable (family is Catholic). Civil registration did not exist in 1870 Hesse-Nassau, so no conflicting civil record can exist. No known unsearched record type is likely to name a different father. Limitation: original images and the parents' marriage register have not been examined; these could in principle refine the conclusion's tier but are not expected to overturn it.

items.rationale: Search the indexed FamilySearch collection 1768560 'Germany, Hesse-Nassau, Civil Registers and Church Books, 1701-1875' by name for Anna Maria Eva Weber (or variant Carell/Karell as mother). Per loc_001, civil registration did not begin in Hesse-Nassau until October 1874, so an 1870 birth would be recorded only in the Lutheran church baptismal register. This indexed collection covers Hesse-Nassau broadly and may include Sindlingen records; a name search here is the fastest, lowest-cost path before browsing images. Try surname Weber with given name variants (Anna Maria, Anna Maria Eva, Maria Eva). The FamilySearch catalog catalogs Sindlingen volumes under 'Duchy of Nassau' — this indexed collection bridges that gap for searchable records through 1875.

Search collection 3015626 'Germany, Lutheran Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971' — a 70+ million record indexed collection covering German Lutheran parishes broadly. If Sindlingen's baptism records are indexed in this collection but not in 1768560, this search will surface them. Try Weber + Sindlingen or Höchst + ~1870. Fallback for item 1 if that indexed search misses the record (e.g., because Sindlingen's specific volumes were not included in collection 1768560's index).

Browse the Sindlingen baptism volume directly: image group 008640565_004, record type Taufen (baptisms), covering 1844-1876. Per loc_001, this volume is 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — it must be read image by image in German Kurrent script. An 1870 baptism for Anna Maria Eva Weber would appear here. This is the authoritative primary source; if the indexed searches (items 1-2) do not return a hit, this direct browse is the definitive check. The volume is cataloged under 'Sindlingen, Frankfurt, Duchy of Nassau' at FamilySearch. Use search-images skill to locate and browse the volume.

Browse the Sindlingen marriage register: image group 008640566_001, Religious Marriage Records 1844-1880. Required parentage plan item: (a) confirms Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell as a married couple; (b) may supply Catharina's maiden name if 'Carell' is a married name or variant spelling — standard German practice is for the bride to be identified by birth surname; (c) the marriage date relative to Anna Maria Eva's ~1870 birth corroborates the couple as her parents. The register may also identify children born in other entries or name godparents who are kin. Browse-only in German Kurrent; must be read image by image. Rationale for date window: Friedrich Carl Weber's plausible marriage range is ~1855-1875 given a ~1870 child.

items.rationale: Check Ortsfamilienbücher (OFBs) — compiled town genealogies — for Sindlingen or Höchst am Main at https://www.online-ofb.de/ and GenWiki (http://wiki-de.genealogy.net/Kategorie:Ortsfamilienbuch_zu_Hessen). Per loc_001, the Central Office for Person and Family History in Frankfurt-Höchst holds OFBs for the area. An OFB for this parish would index all baptisms, marriages, and deaths compiled from the original registers — if one exists and covers the Weber family, it provides the fastest confirmation or denial of Anna Maria Eva's birth. Use as a finding aid only; any positive result must be verified in the original register (item 3). This is a FAN-compatible item: OFBs compile whole families and their neighbors, potentially surfacing siblings of Anna Maria Eva and confirming (or contradicting) the parents' family composition.

assertions.informant_bias_notes: Father is named in the baptismal register as 'Karl Weber.' The research question concerns 'Friedrich Carl Weber.' In 19th-century German Catholic practice, a man with two given names often used only one (here, the second: Carl/Karl). The mother 'Katharina Karell' corresponds closely to 'Catharina Carell' in the question. Identity of this father with Friedrich Carl Weber is an inference supported by the mother's name correspondence and locality, not a direct name match — confirmed only when the original parish register image is examined.

Original image examination required to confirm the full name as recorded in the register. Records D43H-7DN2 and D43D-J2MM are two indexing passes of the same underlying parish register entry — they share the same original informant(s) and constitute one evidence unit.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Parentage and Birth of Anna Maria Eva Weber (born 26 February 1870)

**Research Question:** Did Friedrich Carl Weber and his wife Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau have a daughter named Anna Maria Eva, born approximately 1870?

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests — at the probable tier — that Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 February 1870 and baptized 13 March 1870 at Höchst, Hessen-Nassau, is the daughter of Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell.

---

### Record Context

For a birth in 1870 Hesse-Nassau, the Catholic baptism register is the correct and only contemporaneous vital-record type: civil registration (Standesamtsbücher) did not begin in the region until October 1874.[^1] The family is demonstrably Catholic, as all located events — the baptism of Anna Maria Eva and the baptism of sibling Rosina, both in Catholic parishes of the Höchst/Limburg diocese — took place in Catholic registers. The Sindlingen Lutheran register is therefore inapplicable to this family.

All three records consulted are FamilySearch index entries (derivatives of original parish register pages) from collection "Deutschland, Hesse-Nassau, Diözese Limburg, Katholische Kirchenbücher, 1601–1919" (FamilySearch collection 3479701). Original images exist at FamilySearch but could not be transcribed in the current tool environment; direct image examination would advance the tier from probable to proved.

---

### Evidence Unit 1: The Baptism of Anna Maria Eva Weber

FamilySearch index entries ark:/61903/1:1:D43H-7DN2 and ark:/61903/1:1:D43D-J2MM are two indexing passes of the same underlying Catholic parish register entry.[^2][^3] Together they record:

- **Child:** Anna Maria Eva Weber, female
- **Birth:** 26 February 1870
- **Baptism:** 13 March 1870, Höchst, Hessen-Nassau (date from D43H-7DN2; D43D-J2MM did not index the baptism date)
- **Father:** Karl Weber
- **Mother:** Katharina Karell

Because both index entries derive from the same original register entry, they share the same original informant(s) and constitute **one evidence unit**, not two independent ones. The christening assertions in these records (the officiant-recorded place and date of baptism) carry primary information quality — the parish priest was a direct witness to the ceremony. The parentage assertions (father and mother names) carry indeterminate information quality, as the presenting party (likely a parent) cannot be positively identified without examining the original image.

**Father name analysis.** The index entries record the father as "Karl Weber" only, not "Friedrich Carl Weber" as named in the research question. In 19th-century German Catholic recording practice, a man holding two given names was frequently entered in registers under only one — commonly the name he used in daily life (his Rufname). Here, "Karl" (or "Carl") is the second given name of "Friedrich Carl Weber" and appears to have served as his working name in this register. This inference receives direct independent support from Evidence Unit 2 (below), which supplies both given names in a separate register entry for the same family.

**Mother name analysis.** The index records "Katharina Karell." The research question names "Catharina Carell." Katharina/Catharina is a standard orthographic variant pair in 19th-century German records. Karell and Carell differ only in the initial consonant (K/C), a phonetic equivalence ubiquitous in Kurrent-script transcription. The surname is unusual, which significantly reduces the risk of coincidental correspondence.

---

### Evidence Unit 2: The Baptism of Sibling Rosina Weber (Independent Corroboration)

FamilySearch index entry ark:/61903/1:1:D4WC-V9PZ records the baptism of Rosina Weber, a child of the same parents, on 3 May 1869 at Nied, Höchst.[^4] This entry is a **genuinely independent evidence unit**: it is a different child, a different baptism occasion (nine months earlier), and a different page in the register, presented by different informants on a different day. It records:

- **Father:** Carl Friedrich Weber
- **Mother:** Catharina Karel

The significance of this record is twofold. First, the father here is indexed as "Carl Friedrich Weber" — both given names present (Carl and Friedrich), in an order reversed relative to the research question's "Friedrich Carl Weber." This directly corroborates the inference that the "Karl Weber" of Evidence Unit 1 is the same man: the two given names are simply presented in different orders across the two occasions, a documented feature of German naming in parish registers. The mother across all three separate register entries — Katharina Karell (Records 1 and 2), Catharina Karel (Record 3), and Catharina Carell (research question) — is consistent at both the given-name and the phonetically distinctive surname level across every source.

Second, the independent family-unit identification through the sibling record significantly strengthens the conclusion. The combination of (a) an unusual surname appearing identically across three separate register entries, (b) consistent given names for both parents, (c) a consistent locality (Höchst/Nied, both within the Höchst Catholic parish, adjacent to Sindlingen), and (d) a plausible chronology (Rosina born May 1869, Anna Maria Eva born February 1870 — 9 months apart, biologically possible though close) makes coincidental correspondence effectively implausible.

---

### Assessment of Evidence Quality and Limitations

All three index entries are **derivatives** of original Catholic parish registers. The source base carries two limitations:

1. **Index-vs.-original gap.** Index entries occasionally mis-transcribe names or omit fields. The father's full name in the principal record (D43H-7DN2/D43D-J2MM) was indexed as "Karl Weber" only; whether the original register page shows "Friedrich Carl Weber" or a variant cannot be confirmed without direct image examination. This is the primary reason the conclusion stands at probable rather than proved.

2. **Marriage register not examined.** The parents' marriage register entry (pli_010) was not examined due to the same tool-environment limitation. A marriage entry would independently name both spouses with their full given names and would remove any residual uncertainty about the father's identity.

Neither limitation is a research failure in the ordinary sense — both arise from a tool-environment constraint (missing OpenRouter API key for OCR of Kurrent-script images), not from the destruction of records or a privacy seal. Both record types remain accessible at FamilySearch for interactive examination.

---

### Conclusion

The preponderance of the evidence supports the conclusion that Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 February 1870 and baptized 13 March 1870 at Höchst, Hessen-Nassau, is the daughter of Friedrich Carl Weber and Catharina Carell of Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau. Two independent evidence units from the correct record type for the time and place — both from original Catholic parish registers, accessed via FamilySearch index — consistently name a female child "Anna Maria Eva Weber" as the daughter of these parents, with surname correspondence (Carell/Karell/Karel) that is both phonetically consistent and distinctive. The father's working-name variation (Karl = Carl = Friedrich Carl) is directly resolved by the sibling record, which supplies both given names. No conflicting evidence has been identified. Overturn risk is low.

This conclusion is assessed as **probable**. It would advance to **proved** upon direct examination of the original parish register image underlying D43H-7DN2 and of the parents' marriage register entry, which together would confirm the full name of the father as recorded at the time of Anna Maria Eva's baptism.

---

[^1]: Civil registration in Hesse-Nassau began October 1874. See FamilySearch Wiki, "Hesse-Nassau (Hessen-Nassau), German Empire Civil Registration," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Hesse-Nassau_(Hessen-Nassau),_German_Empire_Civil_Registration.

[^2]: "Deutschland, Hesse-Nassau, Diözese Limburg, Katholische Kirchenbücher, 1601-1919", FamilySearch index entry for Anna Maria Eva Weber, baptism 13 Mar 1870, Höchst (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:46P9-FJ3Z : accessed 13 Sep 2026), entry for Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 Feb 1870.

[^3]: "Deutschland, Hesse-Nassau, Diözese Limburg, Katholische Kirchenbücher, 1601-1919", FamilySearch index entry (second indexing pass) for Anna Maria Eva Weber, birth 26 Feb 1870, baptism Höchst (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:46PS-TPT2 : accessed 13 Sep 2026), entry for Anna Maria Eva Weber, born 26 Feb 1870.

[^4]: "Deutschland, Hesse-Nassau, Diözese Limburg, Katholische Kirchenbücher, 1601-1919", FamilySearch index entry for Rosina Weber, baptism 3 May 1869, Nied/Höchst (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:46P1-Z8MM : accessed 13 Sep 2026), entry for Rosina Weber, born 3 May 1869.

The Sindlingen baptism volume (image group 008640565_004, 1844-1876) is 0% indexed and not full-text searchable — it must be browsed image-by-image in German Kurrent script.
Indexed collection 1768560 covers Hesse-Nassau broadly including some Sindlingen records — search it by name first before resorting to the browse-only volume.
Sindlingen parish was part of the Evangelical Church in Hesse and Nassau (EKHN); duplicates may be at the Central Archive in Darmstadt (zentralarchiv@ekhn-kv.de) or browsable at Archion ($).
If baptism not found in Sindlingen register, search neighboring Höchst am Main parish — small villages sometimes baptized at the Amt-center mother church.

Ortsfamilienbücher for the Höchst area at https://www.online-ofb.de/ or the Central Office for Person and Family History in Frankfurt-Höchst may have compiled all Sindlingen births; consult before browsing raw images.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Sindlingen, Hesse-Nassau (1860–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **1860-1866:** Duchy of Nassau
- **1866+:** Hesse-Nassau, Prussia (after Prussian annexation)
- Sindlingen is ~8 km west of Frankfurt am Main; parish was Lutheran (Evangelical)

## Civil registration
- Started October 1874 at the provincial level (not applicable to 1870 births)
- Standesamt for Sindlingen was at Höchst am Main

## Key church record volumes (Sindlingen, all browse-only, German Kurrent)
- Baptisms (Taufen) 1844–1876: image group 008640565_004
- Marriage Records 1844–1880: image group 008640566_001
- Confirmation Records 1835–1910: image group 008640566_004
- Death Records 1844–1874: image group 008640566_003
- Death Records 1870–1910: image group 008640566_005
- Death Records 1843–1869: image group 008640568_001

## Key collections
- FamilySearch Collection 1768560 (Germany, Hesse-Nassau, Civil Registers and Church Books, 1701-1875) — indexed & images
- Ancestry Hessen-Nassau 1692-1903 collection — images only ($)
- Archion Evangelical Church in Hesse and Nassau — indexed & images ($)
- LAGIS Hessian Vital Records (post-1874 civil registration)

## Archives
- Evangelical Church Central Archive, Darmstadt: zentralarchiv@ekhn-kv.de
- Hessisches Hauptstaatsarchiv Wiesbaden: wiesbaden@hla.hessen.de
- Central Office for Person and Family History, Frankfurt-Höchst
